# 1f Health and stats: contract

**Read first:** [server health](../processes/servers/server-health.md), [server stats](../processes/servers/server-stats.md), [check-host.net](../integrations/check-host.md), [ADR 0005](../adr/0005-home-is-the-russian-vantage-point.md), [events → Servers](../events.md#servers), [open questions](../open-questions.md) "To verify" 3 and 8, designs `RP-Server-health`, `RP-Server-stats`, `RP-Pause-checks`, `RP-Dashboard-ok`, `RP-Dashboard-offline`, `RP-Dashboard-first-run`, the 1c–1e **As built** notes.

**Done when:** every active server is checked on schedule (self-check with stats, proxy test per endpoint, check-host.net external checks, the reference check of home); the verdict rules, flap protection, freezing, on-demand external checks, pause/resume and reminders work exactly as the health doc says; the Health and Stats tabs and the dashboard show it; stats are collected, rolled up and pruned; every checklist line has its test.

## Decisions

| Topic | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Schedules | `servers.reference` every 1 min; `servers.round` every 5 min; `servers.external_round` every 30 min; `servers.checkhost_nodes` daily at 04:10; `servers.reminders` every 1 h; `servers.stats_rollup` every 1 h. All jitter 0 except `servers.round` and `servers.external_round` (10 % jitter). | health.md table. |
| Round | `servers.round` enqueues, per **active, non-paused, non-retiring** server: `servers.selfcheck` now (resource key `server:<id>`, `SkipIfBusy`) and `servers.proxytest` with `Delay` 150 s (**no** resource key, no `SkipIfBusy`); both with coalescing key `<type>:<id>` and `Quiet`. When it starts, the proxy test job calls `jobs.System.Busy(ctx, "server:<id>")` (new platform helper: a `running` job holds the key) and, when busy, stores nothing, evaluates nothing and ends ("skipped: <job> is running"). A skipped self-check enqueue changes nothing either. | "Offset from the self-check"; a running redeploy must not count against health. `SkipIfBusy` counts queued jobs, so the proxy test can't use it next to the self-check it was queued with. |
| Reference job | `servers.reference` does nothing when no server is active and unpaused. Otherwise GET each domestic and foreign reference (5 s each, in parallel, any 2xx/3xx/204 counts); any one per side is enough. Stores a result; on a state change updates `servers_home` and records `health.home_offline` / `health.foreign_unreachable` / `health.home_recovered{duration}` on subject `home:1`. | health.md "home connectivity". |
| Self-check job | `servers.selfcheck`: one connection, `remote.SelfCheck(checks, thresholds from settings)` then `remote.Stats(dir)`; store the self result (`ok` / `stack-failed` with the failing checks / `unreachable` with the SSH error class / `host-key-changed`); store the sample (1f stats rules); raise `cert_expiring` / `disk_low` (below); evaluate. | |
| Proxy test job | `servers.proxytest`: `proxy.Test` per endpoint (1c options from settings and the template's URL), one result per endpoint; if any fails and no external result newer than `external_on_demand_after` (10 min) exists and the budget allows, enqueue an on-demand `servers.external` (coalescing `external:<id>`) and mark the server `awaiting_external` (in `health_detail`) with the time; evaluate. | health.md "on demand". |
| External job | `servers.external`: no resource key. Budget first, counted on stored non-skipped external rows: scheduled → refused when that server has one newer than 80 % of `external_every` (24 min by default, so a previous result stored late by its own polling never skips the next round); on-demand → refused when it has one newer than `external_on_demand_after`; global ≤ `external_hourly_cap` per rolling hour; over budget → store one `skipped` row and evaluate with "no external data". Then check-host: one request with every configured node, poll every 2 s up to 30 s; store one row per node (`vantage` = node name, `ok`, connect ms or error); check-host errors → one row `vantage = "check-host"`, `ok = 0`, `class = "unavailable"`; evaluate. | check-host.md budget. |
| check-host client | `GET /check-tcp?host=<ip>:443&node=…` and `GET /check-result/<id>` with `Accept: application/json`, `GET /nodes/hosts`; base URL configurable. The response shapes are taken from check-host's documentation **and verified once against the real API during this sub-phase** (open question 3); the fake mirrors what was observed; As built records it. | Open question 3. |
| Nodes | `servers_checkhost_nodes` refreshed daily. Settings `servers.external_nodes_ru` and `servers.external_nodes_abroad` (node names, comma-separated); defaults filled on the first refresh when empty: 3 nodes in RU, 3 in DE/NL/FI (one each, the first by name). Settings → Servers shows them grouped as "Russia" / "abroad" with checkboxes. | check-host.md. |
| Freshness | The evaluation uses, per check, the latest result no older than **2 × its interval** (self 10 min, proxy 10 min per endpoint, external 60 min). Older counts as missing. | health.md "no older than two of its intervals". |
| Verdict | A pure function `health.Evaluate(in CheckState, th, now) Outcome` implementing [the rules below](#verdict-rules) in order. They are health.md's rules 1–10 made complete: every combination of inputs matches exactly one rule (a table test enumerates them). Thresholds: slow = first byte > `slow_first_byte` (2 s) or throughput < `slow_kbps` (1000). Reasons are message keys with arguments, rendered in the admin's language on the page and in notifications. | health.md verdict; the review found inputs no rule matched. |
| Waiting for external | When the candidate would come from a rule that needs "no external data" (8, 10, 11) and `awaiting_external` is younger than 2 min, the evaluation stores nothing (no candidate) and enqueues `servers.evaluate` with `Delay` 2 min (coalescing `evaluate:<id>`). The external job's evaluation, or that delayed one, decides. | health.md "waits up to 2 minutes". |
| Freezing | Reference state not `online` → the evaluation records no candidate and changes nothing; results stored meanwhile are `inconclusive = 1` and are skipped by later evaluations' freshness (an inconclusive result is treated as missing). | "Inconclusive results never count." |
| Counted evaluations | Every result triggers an evaluation, but only a **counted** one moves `candidate`/`candidate_count`: one that sees a proxy-test round newer than `counted_proxy_at` (the newest `at` among the server's fresh proxy results). It sets `counted_proxy_at` to that time. An uncounted evaluation (the self-check's, a scheduled external check's, a second look at the same proxy round) only refreshes `health_detail` and applies immediate outcomes (paused, host key). A waiting evaluation stores nothing, so the external job's or the delayed `servers.evaluate`'s evaluation is the counted one for that round. | Otherwise one failed proxy test and the self-check 150 s later would make "2 consecutive evaluations" from one result. |
| Flap protection | On a counted evaluation: same candidate as before → count + 1, else count = 1. The state changes when count ≥ `flap_confirmations` (2), or at once for `paused`, the host-key case, and the first state after `unknown`. A change sets `health_since`, `health_reason`, resets `reminded_at`, and records `server.health_changed{from, to, reason, summary}`. `health_detail` is updated by every evaluation (the page shows the latest reasons even without a change). | |
| Health notifications | `server.health_changed` has `NotifyIf`: `to ∈ {blocked, down}`, or `to = healthy` and `from ∈ {blocked, down}`. Its renderer writes "🔴 de-1 is down: …", "🟣 nl-2 is blocked: …", "🟢 nl-2 is healthy again". | events.md defaults; activation already says "ready". |
| Reminders | `servers.reminders`: for servers `blocked`/`down` with `health_since` and `reminded_at` (or `health_since`) ≥ 24 h ago → `server.still_unhealthy{state, since}`, `reminded_at = now`. | health.md step 4. |
| Cert and disk | **Once per crossing** (user decision 2026-10-07). From the self-check: `expiring_days < cert_warn_days` (14) and `cert_warned = 0` → `server.cert_expiring{days_left}`, `cert_warned = 1`; when the certificate is renewed (days back ≥ the threshold) → `cert_warned = 0`, no event. Same for disk: `low` and `disk_warned = 0` → `server.disk_low{free_pct}`, set; back above the threshold → cleared. An expired certificate or < 2 % disk still fails the check (health handles it). | |
| Pause | Durations 1 h, 6 h, 24 h, until resumed. One `Write`: cancel a queued `servers.resume` of the server (if any), `health = paused` (applied at once, `server.health_changed{to: paused}`), `checks_paused_until`, `server.checks_paused{until}`, and a delayed `servers.resume` job (`Delay` = duration, **no resource key**, no coalescing; none for "until resumed"). The resume job resumes only when `checks_paused_until` is set and ≤ now; otherwise it does nothing (a later pause or a manual Resume already decided). **Resume** (admin) cancels the queued resume job in the same `Write`. Resuming: `health = unknown`, `candidate_count = 0`, `counted_proxy_at = NULL`, `checks_paused_until = NULL`, `server.checks_resumed`. Rounds skip paused servers. A pause from the server list applies to every selected server (1g). | health.md. A delayed job holding `server:<id>` would make every round skip the server for up to 24 h. |
| Run checks now | Enqueues the self-check (`SkipIfBusy`; when busy the page says "a job is running on this server"), the proxy test (no delay) and an on-demand external (budget applies; when over, the page says so). The Health tab polls every 2 s for 1 min after. | |
| `servers.evaluate` | The delayed re-evaluation: no resource key, coalescing `evaluate:<id>`, `Quiet`. Does nothing for a server that is no longer active or is paused. | |
| Stats batch | `remote.Stats`: one command printing sections: `/proc/loadavg`, `/proc/stat` first line, `/proc/meminfo` (`MemTotal - MemAvailable` = used), `df -P -B1 /`, `ip route show default` (device) and `/proc/net/dev`, `/proc/uptime`, `docker ps -a --filter label=com.docker.compose.project.working_dir=<dir> --format json` (name, state, restart count via `docker inspect` in the same command). Parsed into a sample. | stats.md step 1. |
| Deltas | CPU % and traffic from the previous sample of that server when (a) it exists, (b) uptime grew, (c) counters didn't go down; otherwise NULL (counters stored). | stats.md rules. |
| Rollup | `servers.stats_rollup`: raw samples older than 7 days → hourly rows (averages; traffic sums; `samples` count), then deleted, in batches of 5 000 rows per transaction; hourly rows older than 90 days deleted; check results and reference results older than 30 days deleted. | data-model retention. |
| Gaps | Charts break the line where samples are missing (gap > 2 × interval); never zero-filled. | stats.md. |
| Display time | "Traffic today" and "this month" use the display time zone's day and month boundaries converted to UTC for the query. | stats.md. |
| Charts | Platform `ui.Sparkline(points)`, `ui.TimeSeries(series, range)`, `ui.Bar(used, total)` render SVG on the server (viewBox, no inline style; classes from `tokens.css`), nulls break the path. Ranges 24 h (raw), 7 d (raw), 30 d (hourly). | No JS chart library under the CSP. |
| Dashboard | Servers area: banners for home `offline` / `foreign-unreachable`; counts by health; every non-healthy active server with its reason and since; servers with "update available"; top 3 by disk use and by traffic today; the first-run checklist items owned by servers (Cloudflare configured, a server exists). | ui/README dashboard. |
| Queue | `checks` (8 workers, 0c). All check jobs `Quiet`, `MaxAttempts 1`. | |

## Verdict rules

Evaluated top to bottom; the first match gives the candidate. "Pass" means within the thresholds unless it says "any speed". The self-check is `ok`, `stack-failed`, `unreachable`, or **missing** (no fresh, conclusive result: skipped or stale). External data is **none** (no fresh result, or check-host unavailable), or the count of nodes abroad that connected. Rules marked † are new compared with health.md; the others are its rules with their conditions made explicit.

| # | Condition | Candidate | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Checks paused | `paused` (at once) | "Checks paused until 18:00" |
| 2 | Home state not `online` | frozen: nothing stored | "Home internet is offline … verdict on hold" |
| 2a | Latest self-check class `host-key-changed` | `unknown` (at once) | "Host key changed — accept or investigate" |
| 3 | No fresh proxy result for some endpoint | `unknown` | "Waiting for the first checks" |
| 4 | Every endpoint passes; self-check `ok` or missing | `healthy` | — |
| 5 | At least one endpoint passes (any speed), and: one is slow, or some fail, or the self-check is `stack-failed` | `degraded` | "Slow: 2.4 s to first byte" / "Endpoint backup fails" / "certbot container not running" |
| 5a† | Every endpoint passes (any speed); self-check `unreachable` | `degraded` | "The proxy works, but SSH is unreachable from home" |
| 6 | Every endpoint fails; self-check `stack-failed` | `down` | "Stack broken: xray container not running" |
| 7 | Every endpoint fails; ≥ 1 node abroad connects | `blocked` | "Reachable from Germany and Finland, but the proxy fails from home (stalled after 16 KB); 0/3 Russian nodes connect" |
| 8 | Every endpoint fails; self-check `ok`; external none | `blocked` | "The server is healthy, but the proxy fails from home (unconfirmed from abroad)" |
| 8a† | Every endpoint fails; self-check `ok`; 0 nodes abroad connect | `down` | "The stack runs, but the server is unreachable from home and from 3/3 nodes abroad" |
| 9 | Every endpoint fails; self-check `unreachable`; 0 nodes abroad connect | `down` | "Unreachable from home and from 3/3 nodes abroad" |
| 10 | Every endpoint fails; self-check `unreachable`; external none | `down` | "Unreachable from home (unconfirmed from abroad)" |
| 11† | Anything else (every endpoint fails, self-check missing, no node abroad connects) | `unknown` | "Not enough data: <what is missing>" |

health.md's rule 5 said "or the self-check is `stack-failed`" without requiring a passing endpoint, which would have caught rule 6's case first; 5 now requires one.

## Go signatures

```go
package health

type CheckState struct {
	Self      *SelfResult             // nil = missing or stale
	Proxy     map[string]ProxyResult  // by endpoint key; a missing key = missing
	Endpoints []string                // the server's endpoint keys
	External  *ExternalResult         // nil = no external data
	Home      string                  // online foreign-unreachable offline
	Paused    bool
	PausedUntil time.Time
	AwaitingExternal time.Time        // zero = not waiting
}
type Outcome struct {
	Frozen    bool
	Wait      bool   // waiting for an external check
	Candidate string // healthy degraded blocked down unknown paused
	Immediate bool   // applies without confirmation
	Reason    Reason // message key + args
	Summary   map[string]any
}
func Evaluate(in CheckState, th Thresholds, now time.Time) Outcome
// Apply runs the flap rule and writes the state in tx.
func (s *Service) Apply(ctx context.Context, tx *sqlx.Tx, serverID int64, o Outcome, actor string) (changed bool, err error)

func (s *Service) Pause(ctx context.Context, serverIDs []int64, d time.Duration, untilResumed bool, actor string) error
func (s *Service) Resume(ctx context.Context, serverID int64, actor string) error
func (s *Service) RunNow(ctx context.Context, serverID int64, actor string) error
func (s *Service) JobTypes() []jobs.Type
func (s *Service) Schedules() []jobs.Schedule
```

```go
package checkhost

type Node struct{ Name, Country, City string }
type NodeResult struct {
	Node      string
	OK        bool
	ConnectMS int
	Error     string
}
type Client struct{ BaseURL string; HTTP *http.Client; Poll, Wait time.Duration }
func (c *Client) Nodes(ctx context.Context) ([]Node, error)
func (c *Client) CheckTCP(ctx context.Context, hostPort string, nodes []string) ([]NodeResult, error)
```

```go
package stats

type Sample struct { /* the servers_metric_samples columns */ }
func Next(prev *Sample, cur remote.StatsReading) Sample // deltas or NULLs
func (s *Service) Rollup(ctx context.Context) error
func (s *Service) Series(ctx context.Context, serverID int64, r Range) (Series, error)
func (s *Service) TrafficToday(ctx context.Context, serverID int64) (rx, tx int64, err error)
```

## Routes

| Method, path | What |
|---|---|
| `GET /servers/:id/health` | Verdict, matrix (home, self-check per template check, proxy per endpoint with timings, each RU node, each node abroad: result, time, 24 h sparkline), timeline (`?range=24h|7d|30d`, from `server.health_changed` events of the server), **Run checks now**, **Pause checks** / **Resume** |
| `POST /servers/:id/checks/run` | Run now |
| `GET /servers/:id/pause`, `POST /servers/:id/pause` | Pause dialog / apply |
| `POST /servers/:id/resume` | Resume |
| `GET /servers/:id/stats?range=…` | Charts, current values, uptime, traffic this month, containers |

## Events

Recorded: `server.health_changed` (NotifyIf, renderer), `server.still_unhealthy`, `server.cert_expiring`, `server.disk_low`, `server.checks_paused`, `server.checks_resumed`, `health.home_offline` (off), `health.foreign_unreachable` (on), `health.home_recovered` (on).

## Doc changes in the same commit

- `docs/processes/servers/server-health.md`: the verdict table replaced by [Verdict rules](#verdict-rules) (host key as 2a, 5a, 8a, 11, rule 5 needing a passing endpoint); flap protection counts one evaluation per proxy-test round; the "back to healthy" notification only from blocked/down; the waiting mechanism; pause end via a delayed job that checks the stored time; the proxy test skips itself when a job runs on the server.
- `docs/integrations/check-host.md` and `docs/open-questions.md` (question 3): the observed API.
- `docs/events.md`: `server.health_changed` NotifyIf as above; `server.cert_expiring` and `server.disk_low` once per crossing (was "once a day").

## Checklist

Verdict, in `health/evaluate_test.go` (table-driven over `Evaluate`, plus `Apply` with a DB):

- [x] New active server, first proxy test passes, self-check ok → `healthy` at once — `TestFirstStateAfterUnknownIsImmediate`
- [x] Healthy, one failed proxy test, then the round's self-check (evaluating the same failed result), then a passing proxy test → still `healthy`, `candidate_count` never reached 2 — `TestOneFailureDoesNotFlip`
- [x] Every combination of proxy (all pass / slow / some fail / all fail / missing), self-check (ok / stack-failed / unreachable / missing / host key) and external (none / 0 / ≥ 1 abroad) matches exactly one rule — `TestEveryInputHasAVerdict`
- [x] Proxy passes, SSH unreachable → `degraded` ("SSH is unreachable"), no notification — `TestProxyWorksWithoutSSHIsDegraded`
- [x] Proxy fails, self-check ok, 0/3 abroad → `down` ("the stack runs, but…") — `TestStackRunsButUnreachableIsDown`
- [x] Proxy fails, self-check missing, no external → `unknown` ("not enough data") — `TestNotEnoughDataIsUnknown`
- [x] Two evaluations: stall after 16 KB, self ok, 2/3 abroad connect → `blocked` with the stall in the reason; one notification — `TestBlockedAfterTwoEvaluations`
- [x] Proxy fails, self ok, check-host disabled → `blocked (unconfirmed)` after two evaluations — `TestBlockedUnconfirmed`
- [x] Proxy fails, SSH times out, 0/3 abroad → `down` ("unreachable") — `TestDownUnreachable`
- [x] Proxy fails, SSH works, xray exited → `down` ("stack broken: xray container not running") — `TestDownStackBroken`
- [x] Proxy passes with 2.4 s first byte → `degraded`, no notification — `TestDegradedSlow`
- [x] Proxy passes, certbot down → `degraded` ("certbot container not running") — `TestDegradedStackPart`
- [x] Two endpoints, one fails → `degraded` ("Endpoint backup fails") — `TestDegradedOneEndpoint`
- [x] Certificate with 10 days → `healthy` plus one `server.cert_expiring`; no second one while still under 14 days; renewed then under 14 again → a new one — `TestCertExpiringOncePerCrossing`
- [x] Disk under 10 % → one `server.disk_low`; recovers and drops again → another — `TestDiskLowOncePerCrossing`
- [x] Home domestic fails → every verdict frozen, `health.home_offline`, no server changes or notifies — `TestHomeOfflineFreezes`
- [x] Foreign references fail → frozen, one `health.foreign_unreachable`; back → `health.home_recovered` — `TestForeignUnreachableAndRecovery`
- [x] After recovery, the first failing evaluation is only a candidate; the second changes state; inconclusive results don't count — `TestRecoveryNeedsTwoFreshEvaluations`
- [x] Blocked for 25 h → one `server.still_unhealthy` at 24 h — `TestStillUnhealthyReminder`
- [x] A redeploy running when the round is due → skipped, state unchanged — `round_test.go` `TestRoundSkipsBusyServer`
- [x] An idle server's round runs both the self-check and, 150 s later, the proxy test (the queued self-check doesn't make the proxy test skip); a redeploy running when the proxy test starts → it stores nothing — `round_test.go` `TestRoundRunsBothChecks`
- [x] Pause 24 h, Resume by hand, pause 1 h → resumes after 1 h, not 24 h; the old resume job does nothing — `pause_test.go` `TestManualResumeCancelsResumeJob`
- [x] Pause 1 h → `paused` at once, no checks for an hour, then `unknown`, then a verdict from new results — `pause_test.go` `TestPauseForAnHour`
- [x] Proxy fails, last external 25 min old → on-demand external starts; evaluation waits for it, at most 2 min — `external_test.go` `TestOnDemandExternalIsAwaited`
- [x] check-host answers with an error → "no external data", reason "unconfirmed" — `external_test.go` `TestCheckHostErrorIsUnconfirmed`
- [x] Budget: a second on-demand within 10 min and the hourly cap → `skipped` rows; a scheduled check 29 min 50 s after a result stored late still runs — `external_test.go` `TestExternalBudget`
- [x] `Busy` is true only while a job holding the key is `running` — `internal/platform/jobs/query_test.go` `TestBusyMeansRunning`
- [x] Host key changed → `unknown` with "host key changed", security notification, no `down` — `TestHostKeyChangedIsUnknown`
- [x] Only active servers are evaluated; provisioning/failed/retired never get health — `round_test.go` `TestOnlyActiveServersAreChecked`
- [x] `server.health_changed` notifies for blocked, down, and healthy-from-blocked/down only — `TestHealthNotificationRule`

check-host, in `checkhost/client_test.go`:

- [x] Nodes parsed with countries; a check polls until every node answered or 30 s — `TestCheckTCPPolls`
- [x] Mixed node answers (time, timeout, refused, still null at the deadline) → per-node results — `TestNodeAnswers`

## As built

Done 2026-10-08. Every checklist line has its test, in the file the line names, except the manual one (see below). `make test` and the pages, health, stats, checkhost, remote and jobs tests are green under `-race`; the `make check`, `make lint` and `docker build .` results are in the commit's report. Deviations and notes for 1g and later:

- **Packages.** `servers/health` (`evaluate.go` the pure verdict and `stack.go`; `service.go` settings, `Load`, `Evaluate`; `apply.go` `Apply`, reasons, `Detail`; `jobs.go` the job types, schedules and the round; `checks.go` the self-check and proxy test jobs; `reference.go`; `external.go` budget, nodes and defaults; `pause.go` Pause, Resume, RunNow; `reminders.go`), `servers/checkhost` (+ `checkhosttest.Fake`), `servers/stats` (`collect.go` `Next`, `rollup.go`, `query.go`), `remote/stats.go` (`CmdStats`, `ParseStats`, `Stats`), `store/health.go` and `store/stats.go` (every statement), `deploy/checks.go` (`CheckSetup`: renders the version in force, so the checks, the stack directory and the proxy test URL are the template's), pages `health.go`, `stats.go`, `dashboard.go`, `server_health.templ`, `server_stats.templ`, `pause.templ`, `messages_health.go`.
- **Platform.** `jobs.System.Busy` as contracted, plus `BusyExcept(ctx, key, types…)` and `CancelQueued(ctx, tx, type, subject, by)` (cancels the unstarted jobs of a type and subject inside the caller's transaction, which a pause needs). `ui.TimeSeries(series, range)`, `ui.Sparkline`, `ui.Strip` (a row of ok/fail/none cells), `ui.Bar`, `ui.Timeline` (coloured stretches) and `ui.BoolStr`; charts are SVG with classes only (`.chart`, `.chart-line`, `.strip-ok`, `.tl-blocked` … in `app.css`), no inline style. `serverstest.VPS` answers the stats batch (`SetMetrics`, `Metrics`), `storetest.Env` has `AddServer`, `Vault`, `Settings`.
- **The proxy test's Busy check ignores the round's own self-check** (`BusyExcept(…, "servers.selfcheck")`). With the self-check holding `server:<id>`, a proxy test queued with no delay (Run checks now, the round after a resume) would always have skipped itself. Any other running job on the server still makes it skip.
- **Signatures that changed.** `Outcome` also carries `Rule`, `ProxyRound` (the newest fresh proxy result, which decides whether an evaluation is counted) and `Summary`. `Apply` is as contracted. `RunNow` returns `(RunResult, error)` (`Busy`, `OverBudget`). `stats.Next(prev, cur, at)` takes the time; `Service.Store(ctx, tx, serverID, at, reading)` writes a sample inside the self-check's transaction. `health.Service.Config(ctx)` reads every setting at once. `Setup` (`Server`, `Dir`, `Checks`, `ProxyTestURL`) is how health gets the template's side; the module adapts `deploy.CheckSetup` to it.
- **Reasons are stored as keys.** `servers_servers.health_reason` and `Detail.Reason` hold JSON `{"key","args"}`; the pages and notifications render them in the admin's language (`health.RenderReason`; arguments `until`, `countries` and `seconds` are formatted there). The event `server.health_changed` carries `from`, `to`, `reason` (rendered in English, which the Activity page shows as it is), `reason_key`, `reason_args` and `summary`. The notification for it is the module's own: "🔴 de-1 is down", "🟣 nl-2 is blocked" with the reason as body, "🟢 nl-2 is healthy again" (`Module.RenderNotification`).
- **The wait for an external check is race-free.** A waiting verdict re-reads the "awaiting" mark inside the write that queues the delayed `servers.evaluate`; the external check clears the mark and cancels the queued evaluation in one transaction. So an answer that arrives while the verdict is being made never leaves a stray job, and the verdict is decided at once.
- **A home outage clears every server's candidate run** when home comes back (`store.ResetCandidates`), so a failure counted before the outage cannot be the first of the "two fresh evaluations".
- **Freshness is per check**: self-check and proxy test 2 × `servers.selfcheck_every`, external 2 × `servers.external_every`. A result whose latest row is inconclusive counts as missing. `servers.external_round` spreads the servers' scheduled external checks 10 s apart.
- **check-host (open question 3).** Verified on 2026-10-08 against the real API: `/nodes/hosts` (about 55 nodes; 3 in Russia: ru1–ru3; none in Finland, so the defaults abroad are the first node by name of de, nl, fi, then se, pl, fr … until three), `/check-tcp` to `1.1.1.1:443` from ru1–ru3, de1, nl1 (all connected, `time` in seconds), to a black-holed address (`Connection timed out` after about 2 polls) and to `127.0.0.1:443` (`Connection refused`). A result is `null` while a node works. The shapes are in [the integration doc](../integrations/check-host.md#api-as-observed) and `checkhosttest.Fake` serves exactly those. Not done: a check of a provisioned server (none exists here), and the service's rate limits and terms stay unknown (open question 3 says so).
- **Settings → Servers** shows the 15 new fields as plain fields; the node lists are comma-separated text, **not** the grouped "Russia / abroad" checkboxes the contract describes. They fill themselves on the first daily node refresh (and when a check finds them empty).
- **Pause dialog** has the four options the health doc names (1 h, 6 h, 24 h, until resumed), not the design's extra "7 days", "until 09:00" and reason field. It is a fragment for htmx (`<dialog data-autoopen>`) and a page for plain GET. A pause from the server list is 1g's (`Service.Pause` already takes many ids).
- **Dashboard.** The servers area holds home's banner (offline, foreign unreachable), the lifecycle counts, the fleet by health, every non-healthy active server with its reason and "since", failed servers, "update available", the top 3 by disk use and by traffic today, and, until Cloudflare is connected and a server exists, the two checklist rows that belong to servers. There is no platform-wide first-run checklist yet; these rows are the servers' part.
- **Not built.** Re-evaluating on `server.redeployed` (the next round does it); the self-check after a change still writes no `servers_check_results` row; the server list's health columns, bars and bulk actions (1g); the `]`/`[` tab keys of the design.
- **Tests.** The health tests drive a full `serverstest.Harness` with a fake clock shared by the health service and the job system (workers are stopped to swap the clock), schedules switched off, a local reference site and a fake check-host. They take about 50 s together under `-race`. No test sleeps more than 60 ms; `TestRoundRunsBothChecks` moves the fake clock 150 s instead of waiting.
- **Not exercised in a real browser:** the Health and Stats tabs, the 2 s polling after Run checks now, the pause dialog, the charts' look (axis labels, strip and timeline colours), the dashboard area. **Not exercised on a real server:** `remote.CmdStats` (its `/proc` parsing is tested against a captured-format sample and the fake VPS, but no real Linux host has answered it; the `docker inspect --format` fields are from its documentation) and the whole health loop against a provisioned VPS and the real Russian vantage point.
- **Notes for 1g.** `store.CheckableServerIDs` already skips servers with `retire_job_id` set, and `Evaluate` ignores them, so retirement only has to set it. A retiring job takes `server:<id>` by waiting; the proxy test skips itself while it runs. `health.Service.Pause(ctx, ids, d, untilResumed, actor)` is the bulk action. `pages.HumanBytes` and the server list can use `stats.Service.Latest` / `TrafficToday` for the mini-bars and the traffic column, and `store.LatestSamples` for all servers at once.
